recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for current core. Do not edit dropped OccupationalData source for this issue unless a human decides to resurrect or republish the artifact in an active FHIR or external ODH specification; any such work should re-review the whole OccupationalData model.
issue_request: FHIR-14743 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 PHER change request for FHIR-core-OccupationalData asking why multiple effective elements used effectiveDateTime/effectivePeriod choices and whether they could be simplified to Period, since an open-ended Period can represent ongoing intervals.
initial_application: Jira records application as svn 13307. Git commit 1834d69412f3ba4890c5930897e1a58b6c98aad0 is svn revision 13307 and explicitly references FHIR-14743/#174 in a Jan 2018 OccupationalData ballot-resolution batch. It changed the example from effectivePeriod elements to effective elements and the spreadsheet records the relevant effective elements as Period.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini comments OccupationalDataforHealth as dropped, so the artifact is outside the current core build. The remaining source/occupationaldata files are inactive and already reflect period-only effective elements. The local FHIR Extension Pack checkout has no OccupationalData definition, and focused Jira/Zulip/Confluence searches found no later or community evidence requiring a current-core edit.
reconciliation: No source was changed. The issue belongs to a dropped/out-of-current-build core artifact, and the inactive source already contains the historical Period-only application.
